notes:
Key points / rep notes:
- Arkadia is finserv-focused, latency = revenue. They run chat + reranking for underwriting flows.
- Primary ask: guaranteed throughput + tight SLOs on p95 for customer-facing chat.
- Disagreement: Arkadia will only accept client-side end-to-end measurement for SLA (includes network, SDK, TLS). Redwood insists on server-side emit for platform-level SLOs and proposes separate E2E objective.
- Streaming vs non-streaming nuance came up: Arkadia measures 'time to first token' + 'time-to-complete-turn' at the client. They want p50/p95/p99 on both metrics. Redwood standard is token-emission latency (server-side) for streaming and full-response latency for non-streaming.
- Quote from CTO: "If our mobile app shows a spinner for >300ms, ops gets paged. We need SLAs that reflect real user experience."
- Legal/billing: prefer annual reserved commit but want 30% cap on penalties for missed SLOs during initial 6 months.
- SE notes: need kernel-level perf breakdown (KV cache warm vs cold) + reserved GPU sku recommendation (8x A10G equiv for initial pool).
- Action items: run 72h and generate alignment report (server vs client percentiles), provide SLA redline v2, finalize GPU sku + headroom plan.
latency_slo_summary: Working SLO targets discussed: Non-streaming (single-turn) — p50 < 120ms server-emit, p95 < 300ms server-emit, p99 < 700ms server-emit. Client E2E negotiation asks: p95 < 350ms end-to-end. Streaming (tokenized) — first-token p50 < 60ms server-emit, first-token p95 < 120ms; per-token p50 < 12ms, p95 < 40ms. Arkadia insists SLOs be measured E2E for SLA; Redwood proposes platform SLOs measured server-side with separate E2E objective for customer experience.
agreed_metrics: Run plan: capture both client-side end-to-end (app SDK timestamps) and server-side emit timestamps in same traces
Define trace alignment: use request_id to correlate client send -> server receive -> first-emit -> final-emit
Compute percentiles separately: p50/p95/p99 for first-token, per-token, full response, and tail-by-payload-size buckets
Streaming rules: measure first-token latency and 95th-percentile per-token delta over steady-state; exclude cold KV-cache warmup window (first 5k requests) from SLA calculation
Non-streaming rules: measure full-response completion time; include network only for E2E SLA; platform SLA will be server-emit only
SLA windowing: 30-day rolling measurement; soft-warning at 3 consecutive days of breach; financial penalties only after remediation window and if monthly breach >1%
